title: Endgame checklist and self-test
outcomes: Rates honestly which endgame lessons can be done without hints and which need another visit
Classifies unlabeled endings from three families (pawn, rook and queen, minor pieces) as won, drawn or lost
Explains why each lesson teaches a principle with a failing look-alike, not a position to memorise

steps.text: This lesson teaches no new ending. It is a **checklist** built from the endgame lessons in this course. Each lesson teaches a principle, positions that win, and a look-alike that fails. Rate yourself honestly first, then test yourself on positions with no label: nothing tells you which lesson applies.

steps.prompt: Pawn endings. For each lesson, rate how well you could do it today without hints.

fields.label: Opposition: one tempo between a win and a draw
Distant opposition: the same fight from afar
Key squares: where the king must get to
Spare moves: who runs out first?
Pawn-step timing: one step or two
Triangulation: a king detour that passes the move
The outside passed pawn: a decoy for the enemy king
The remote passed pawn: bring the king first
Pawn races: the square, and who queens first
The pawn breakthrough: giving pawns to make a passed pawn

steps.text: **Rook and queen endings next.** The lessons below hold the skeletons: the Lucena win and the Philidor defence, the four habits and where they fail, the rook pawn, the pawn on the seventh against the queen, and the fortress. Rate them, then test yourself. Rule of thumb: when a rook ending looks equal, name the skeleton before you calculate.

steps.prompt: Rook, queen and fortress lessons. Rate yourself.

fields.label: Lucena and Philidor: the two rook endings to know
Rook endings: four habits and where they fail
Rook pawns: the corner draw and its limits
Rook and pawn against rook: cut the king off
Queen against a pawn on the seventh: when it is only a draw
Fortresses: when more material cannot break through

steps.text: **Minor pieces and mates.** The last group covers bishop against knight, knight endings, the wrong bishop, the armies that can and cannot force mate, bishop and knight, and the choice of which ending to enter. A look-alike can be a different result with one piece moved. Rate, then test yourself on the last positions.

steps.prompt: Minor-piece and mating lessons. Rate yourself.

fields.label: Bishop against knight: count the wings
Knight endings: count the journey
The wrong bishop, and two knights that cannot mate
Which armies can force mate
Bishop and knight against a lone king: the right corner
Which ending to enter: check the trade first
